_readme: The THIRD PriceList (D-170), as it will be submitted to the price topic 0.0.10426551.
It is sequence 2 with ONE field changed: the hbar method's rate.source. §14.3 makes the
schedule the SEQUENCE of messages and the price current at a purchase the latest message
before it, so this supersedes sequence 2 by landing after it, and sequence 2 is not edited.
WHY IT CHANGED, AND IT IS ABOUT REPLAY RATHER THAN ABOUT PRICE. Sequence 2 read HBAR/USD
from api.saucerswap.finance — a DEX spot price. T-P11-4 is the court for what was charged:
'buy_stamp charges what the price message current at the receipt's consensus timestamp
yields'. A Verifier re-running that arithmetic on a rate-priced method needs the rate the
Postmaster read, at the instant it read it — and a DEX spot price cannot be re-obtained at
a past timestamp by anyone. So every rate-priced receipt this deployment produced would be
unreplayable, and P-12 downgrades what cannot be replayed: appraised never exceeds declared,
and non-replayable evidence downgrades, never upgrades. The price would have been right and
unprovable.
Hedera's own exchange rate is CONSENSUS DATA and is on the mirror node, with a timestamp
filter. FETCHED 2026-09-09: GET /api/v1/network/exchangerate?timestamp=<t> returns the rate
record in force at t — {current_rate {cent_equivalent, hbar_equivalent, expiration_time},
next_rate, timestamp} — deterministically, and querying at the returned record's own
timestamp returns that same record. Any stranger with a mirror node and the receipt's
rate.at can obtain exactly what the Postmaster read. That is what makes T-P11-4 checkable.
rate.value is USD per hbar, computed in integers as cent_equivalent / (100 x hbar_equivalent)
and truncated to the scale §14.3's arithmetic uses, so the number in the receipt is the
number the price was divided by and a replay reaches the same tinybar.
rate.at is the CONSENSUS TIMESTAMP of the rate record, not a wall clock — the thing a
Verifier passes back to the mirror. §5.4 types it as a string and constrains it no further,
so no schema moves.
Everything else is sequence 2's, byte for byte: the same stampToken, the same payTo, the
same bundles, the same provisioning {method, unitPrice, registrationFee}. The x402-usdc
method is fixed-priced and reads no rate, so it is untouched.
spec is 0.5.10 because that is the text this message is published under (D-169). _readme is
stripped before canonicalization, exactly as it is for sequences 1 and 2.
